The Fourth Derivative of the Expected Information

Source: R/d34expected_hessian.R
distrib_d4expected_hessian.Rd

Returns \(\partial^4\,\mathbb{E}[\ell_{ab}]/\partial\theta_c\, \partial\theta_d\,\partial\theta_e\,\partial\theta_f\), with one component per pair \((a,b)\) and per unordered quadruple \((c,d,e,f)\).

Usage

distrib_d4expected_hessian(
  distrib,
  y,
  theta,
  scale = c("parameter", "link"),
  method = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

distrib

A distribution object inheriting from distrib.

y

A numeric vector of observations.

theta

A named list of parameters; each has length 1 or length(y).

scale

"parameter" or "link".

method

NULL (the default) or an object inheriting from ExpectMethod, as for distrib_dexpected_hessian(). An object returns the derivative of the matrix that the method defines, by Leibniz's formula for expect_opg() and with the moved density for expect_integrate() and expect_mc(); with identity = "hessian" the fourth derivative needs observed derivatives of order 6 and signals an error that names identity = "score". See expected_derivative_methods.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

A named list of numeric vectors, keyed as d4expected_names(distrib@params).

Details

The components are symmetric in \((a,b)\) and in \((c,d,e,f)\) separately, and are keyed by d4expected_names().

The univariate families shipped with the package compute the components in closed form, in compiled code. The default method, which serves the wrappers and families defined by the user, applies one second-order central stencil to distrib_d2expected_hessian(): the three-point stencil along one parameter for a repeated pair \((e,e)\), the four-point mixed stencil for two distinct parameters \((e,f)\). It requires a family that registers an analytic second derivative of its expected information and signals an error otherwise. The step is the fourth root of machine epsilon relative to the coordinate, kept inside a finite bound on the parameter scale by fd_steps().

See also

distrib_d2expected_hessian(), distrib_d3expected_hessian(), d4expected_names()

Examples

d <- poisson_distrib()
str(distrib_d4expected_hessian(d, 2, list(mu = 3), scale = "link"))
#> List of 1
#>  $ mu_mu_mu_mu_mu_mu: num -3
